name: Save starred Gmail emails as Markdown notes in Obsidian (via Google Drive)

parameters.content:
## Save the emails that matter as notes in your Obsidian vault — automatically, once a day

### How it works
Star an email in Gmail and this workflow turns it into a clean Markdown note in your Obsidian vault. Once a day it finds every starred email you haven't saved yet and writes each one as a note — a YAML frontmatter block (title, from, date, tags) followed by the body — into a Google Drive folder. Point that folder at your vault's Drive-synced location and the notes just appear in Obsidian. Each saved email is then labelled `obsidian-saved`, which is what keeps the next run from capturing it again.

No Obsidian plugin and no AI key needed — it writes plain `.md` files, so it runs free on n8n Cloud.

### Setup
1. Connect **Gmail** and **Google Drive** (one-click Google sign-in on n8n Cloud).
2. In Gmail, create a label called `obsidian-saved` — the "already captured" marker.
3. Open **Save note to vault** and pick the Drive folder your vault syncs from.
4. Open **Mark email saved** and select the `obsidian-saved` label. Don't skip this — with no label selected nothing gets marked, and every starred email is saved again the next day.
5. (Optional) In **⚙️ Your settings**, change which emails to capture or the tag added to each note.
6. Activate. It runs daily at 7am.

### Honest notes
Run it once with a single starred email before pointing it at your whole inbox. The label is applied just after the note is written, so if a run dies between those two steps that one email gets a second note tomorrow. Body is plain text (HTML emails are converted to text) — attachments and formatting are not carried over.

## 1. Find emails to save
Runs daily at 7am. Pulls every email that matches your capture rule (default: starred) and isn't already labelled `obsidian-saved` — so each run only ever sees what's new.

## 2. Build the note
Turns each email into a Markdown file: a YAML frontmatter block (title, from, date, tags) followed by the body. Filenames are date-prefixed, cleaned of the characters Obsidian and your OS dislike, and end with a short id so two emails with the same subject never overwrite each other.

## 3. Save + mark done
Writes the note into your vault's Google Drive folder, then labels the email `obsidian-saved`. That label is the guard that makes re-runs safe: a labelled email is skipped from then on. The one gap is the moment between the two steps — a run that dies there leaves the email unlabelled, and tomorrow's run writes a second note of it.
